channel.title: Persistent Volume Claim on KubeSphere
channel.description: Recent content in Persistent Volume Claim on KubeSphere

item.title: Create a Persistent Volume Claim
item.description: This section describes how to create a PersistentVolumeClaim. Prerequisites You need to join a cluster and have the Persistent Volume Claim Management permission in the cluster. For more information, see Cluster Members and Cluster Roles. Steps Log in to the KubeSphere web console with a user who has Persistent Volume Claim Management permissions and enter your cluster. Click Storage > Persistent Volume Claims in the left navigation pane.

item.title: View Persistent Volume Claim List
item.description: This section describes how to view the list of persistent volume claims. Prerequisites You need to join a cluster and have the Persistent Volume Claim View permission in the cluster. For more information, see Cluster Members and Cluster Roles. Steps Log in to the KubeSphere web console with a user who has Persistent Volume Claim View permissions and enter your cluster. Click Storage > Persistent Volume Claims in the left navigation pane.

item.title: View Persistent Volume Claim Details
item.description: This section describes how to view persistent volume claim details. Prerequisites You need to join a cluster and have the Persistent Volume Claim View permission in the cluster. For more information, see Cluster Members and Cluster Roles. Steps Log in to the KubeSphere web console with a user who has Persistent Volume Claim View permissions and enter your cluster. Click Storage > Persistent Volume Claims in the left navigation pane.

item.title: Clone a Persistent Volume Claim
item.description: This section describes how to clone a PersistentVolumeClaim. After a PersistentVolumeClaim and a PersistentVolume are created, you can create identical copies for the PersistentVolumeClaim and the PersistentVolume respectively by cloning. Prerequisites You need to join a cluster and have the Persistent Volume Claim Management permission in the cluster. For more information, see Cluster Members and Cluster Roles. Ensure that the system has created a persistent volume for the persistent volume claim.

item.title: Expand a Persistent Volume Claim
item.description: This section describes how to expand the volume capacity of a PersistentVolumeClaim. The capacity of the bound PersistentVolume will also be expanded accordingly. Prerequisites You need to join a cluster and have the Persistent Volume Claim Management permission in the cluster. For more information, see Cluster Members and Cluster Roles. Ensure that the system has created a persistent volume for the persistent volume claim.

item.title: Edit Persistent Volume Claim Information
item.description: This section describes how to edit the basic information of a PersistentVolumeClaim. You can edit the alias and description of a PersistentVolumeClaim. KubeSphere does not support editing the name of a PersistentVolumeClaim. Prerequisites You need to join a cluster and have the Persistent Volume Claim Management permission in the cluster. For more information, see Cluster Members and Cluster Roles. Steps Log in to the KubeSphere web console with a user who has Persistent Volume Claim Management permissions and enter your cluster.

item.title: Delete Persistent Volume Claim
item.description: This section describes how to delete a PersistentVolumeClaim. Warning A PersistentVolumeClaim cannot be recovered after deletion, and by default, the corresponding PersistentVolume will also be deleted. Please perform this operation with caution to avoid data loss. Prerequisites You need to join a cluster and have the Persistent Volume Claim Management permission in the cluster.

item.title: Create Persistent Volume
item.description: Persistent Volumes (PVs) are the core carriers of cluster storage resources. In addition to being dynamically created through Persistent Volume Claims, they can also be created manually. Prerequisites You need to join a cluster and have the Persistent Volume Claim Management permission in the cluster. For more information, see Cluster Members and Cluster Roles. Steps Log in to the KubeSphere web console with a user who has Persistent Volume Claim Management permissions and enter your cluster.

item.title: View Persistent Volume List
item.description: This section describes how to view the persistent volume list. Prerequisites You need to join a cluster and have the Persistent Volume Claim View permission in the cluster. For more information, see Cluster Members and Cluster Roles. Steps Log in to the KubeSphere web console with a user who has Persistent Volume Claim View permissions and enter your cluster. Click Storage > Persistent Volume Claims in the left navigation pane.

item.title: View Persistent Volume Details
item.description: This section describes how to view the details of a persistent volume in a cluster. Prerequisites You need to join a cluster and have the Persistent Volume Claim View permission in the cluster. For more information, see Cluster Members and Cluster Roles. Steps Log in to the KubeSphere web console with a user who has Persistent Volume Claim View permissions and enter your cluster.

item.title: Edit Persistent Volume Information
item.description: This section describes how to edit the information of a persistent volume. You can edit the alias and description of a persistent volume. KubeSphere does not support editing the name of a persistent volume. Prerequisites You need to join a cluster and have the Persistent Volume Claim Management permission in the cluster. For more information, see Cluster Members and Cluster Roles. Steps Log in to the KubeSphere web console with a user who has Persistent Volume Claim Management permissions and enter your cluster.

item.title: Delete Persistent Volume
item.description: This section describes how to delete a persistent volume. The default reclamation policy for storage classes on the KubeSphere platform is Delete, meaning that by default, the system automatically deletes the persistent volume after the persistent volume claim is deleted. If you have created a persistent volume or storage class with a reclamation policy of Retain, there may be situations where the persistent volume claim is deleted but the persistent volume is not.
